messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — deploy canary (api-service) reporting 500s in us-west-2 after secrets rotation. Summary: prefixed failures across canary pods, error rate ~6%. Paging alice_eng_oncall.

alice_eng_oncall: seeing it, joining. any recent secret/rotation activity?

carla_infra: rotated vault token for the deploy pipeline 10m ago to address expiry. rollout to canary started 8m ago.

bob_sre: getting 502/500 from the canary pods. stack traces show decryption failures: "failed to unwrap key: permission denied".

alice_eng_oncall: can someone paste the pod env and vault status?

carla_infra: quick checks:
```
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=api-service-canary -o wide
NAME                                     READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
api-service-canary-5b6f7    2/2     Running   0          6m
api-service-canary-6c7d8    1/2     CrashLoop  2          5m
```

carla_infra: and env diff between working and failing pod: `VAULT_TOKEN` present in working pod, missing in failing one. Looks like agent restart after rotation didn't pick up new token for one replica.

bob_sre: also seeing permission errors in logs from KMS wrapper: `AccessDeniedException` when trying to decrypt key material. Could be stale IAM role attached to the canary node.

maya_security: confirmed we rotated the key alias last night. New alias requires updated IAM policy allowing kms:Decrypt for the new alias. Deployment role may still reference old alias permissions.

alice_eng_oncall: impact assessment? product?

dave_product: initial customer telemetry shows ~4 customers had failed requests in last 5m. Overall traffic for api-service is healthy, but writing endpoints are erroring for the canary slice. No large-scale data loss.

tony_ops: recommended mitigation options: 1) abort canary rollout 2) toggle feature flag to stop writes 3) rollback to previous deployment image where token handling different.

alice_eng_oncall: I'll abort the canary and flip the kill-switch for writes to be safe. tony_ops, can you prep rollback if abort doesn't help?

carla_infra: aborting canary now: `redwoodctl rollout abort --deployment api-service --target canary` -> returned ok. Observed canary pods terminating.

alice_eng_oncall: flipping feature flag: `featureflag.set api.write_enabled false --scope=canary` -> done. Notifying product.

dave_product: confirmed flag flip, writes disabled for canary users. Customer-facing errors should stop. Creating a banner for affected customers.

bob_sre: monitoring — error rate dropped to baseline within 60s. New spikes gone.

maya_security: we'll update IAM policy and re-issue role permissions to include kms:Decrypt for new alias. Planning a permissions patch and small redeploy to canary with validated role.

alice_eng_oncall: handing off to bob_sre for next 2h rotation to watch for regressions and to carla_infra for rollout of the IAM fix. I'll file postmortem and include timeline + mitigation steps.

bob_sre: taking oncall for follow-up. Adding short runbook: 1) verify node IAM role has kms:Decrypt on alias 2) ensure Vault agent refresh on deployment restart 3) test canary with synthetic traffic before re-enabling writes.

carla_infra: creating patch PR for role policy now. Expect deploy in ~25m after approvals.

alice_eng_oncall: thanks all. will escalate to SEV-incident if we see customer impact >2% or more than 10 customers. For now status: mitigated, degraded.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS UPDATE — mitigated -> monitoring. Tags: feature-flag, secrets, canary, rollback, iam-permissions.

alice_eng_oncall: postmortem owner assigned: alice_eng_oncall. add maya_security and carla_infra as reviewers.

carla_infra: FYI: PR link https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/432 - includes IAM policy change and a validation job for Vault agent presence.

bob_sre: leaving notes for next oncall: check `kubectl describe pod` for EnvFrom mounts and `aws iam get-role-policy` to validate policy includes new alias ARN.

alice_eng_oncall: thanks everyone, closing the noisy alerts. we'll reconvene after patch rollout and canary re-run. :white_check_mark:
